framing: The corpus is part of the model
paragraphs: A filtering change removes noisy pages and raises the average quality score of a training corpus. It also removes useful source code because the rule mistakes symbols for clutter. The resulting dataset looks cleaner by its own metric while becoming less suited to the intended assistant. To detect that tradeoff, the team must retain more than a final token count.

Every stage changes what the model gets to practice. Extraction can lose structure, deduplication can remove coverage, and sampling can amplify a small source through repeated exposure. Even a declared source probability may produce a surprising token share when document lengths differ. These choices affect the meaning of the scaling estimate you just studied, as well as the credibility of later evaluations.

Follow text from its source through extraction, quality checks, duplicate candidates, benchmark screening, tokenization, and packed training blocks. The chapter's small examples make difficult distinctions visible: a similarity chain need not connect mutually similar documents, renamed code can evade literal matching, and a separator does not enforce independent attention. You will also examine restart state and the difference between unique inventory and repeated presentations. Published corpus recipes provide context without becoming universal defaults.

The earlier privacy and governance chapters establish why a source needs permission and an explicit handling policy. The scaling chapter provides a provisional volume target. This chapter connects those decisions to the actual tokens consumed by training. Bring your understanding of tokenization, causal attention, and next-token loss. The upcoming fine-tuning pipeline will reuse the same care with sequence limits, shifting, data lineage, and token positions, but apply it to demonstrations of desired behavior.
outcomes: Explain a corpus change using retained coverage and token yield.
Distinguish duplicate candidates, verified overlap, and residual contamination risk.
Check packed attention, shifted targets, and restart position against the intended objective.
question: Which useful text could your cleaning rules remove, and what evidence would reveal the loss before the full run?
